flash_bytes.reason: +5,088 B over the 4,071,536 B ceiling on origin/main (00b6308c, #199): a cancel (Back or the time budget) is one typed outcome from every cancel point to every consumer, so it never reads as a changed book, a missing page or a ready frame. A cancelled Contents load or jump keeps the reader on its page; the cancelled source stays unreadable until one shared reload runs before every action, repaint and pending verification; the final freshness check runs before the cancel question and a target it refused is discarded. The owner holds one verification authority per open book across every short loan: only a successful hash makes it Verified and a failed re-hash stays failed, so no exit saves a changed book. Firmware reads the descriptor only through that reload gate, the availability probe included. A Contents load and an interrupted staging complete as what they are, a cancelled paint composes nothing for the display or the resume picture, and a cancelled operation closes its Pages scope so a refused index read never reads as damage.
